newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Homeless man sets fire to himself after Yeltsin speaks.
newsitem.headline: Homeless man sets fire to himself after Yeltsin speaks.

text.p: A homeless man set fire to himself on Red Square on Thursday, just 200 metres (yards) from where President Boris Yeltsin had given a keynote Kremlin speech shortly before.

Police said 60-year-old Gennady Yermolov, from a village in the Kirov region northwest of Moscow, was taken to hospital with 20 percent burns, including face and hands, after he poured petrol over himself and lit it in front of St.Basil's Cathedral.
"He could no longer live where he was and saw no prospect of improving his circumstances," a police official told Reuters.
Yeltsin, in a speech three hours before the suicide attempt, said: "People's patience is reaching its limits."
He called for urgent measures to end delays in the payment of pensions and wages and for a major government shake-up.
